38 Two nuclides are different isotopes of the same element.
Which statement about the nuclides is correct?
A
Neutral atoms of the nuclides have the same number of electrons.
B
Nuclei of the nuclides have different numbers of protons.
C
Nuclei of the nuclides have the same number of nucleons.
D
Nuclei of the nuclides have the same number of neutrons.

hints: Notice the wording same element - this fixes the proton number $Z$ for both nuclei.
Recall that isotopes are defined by same $Z$ but different nucleon number $A$ due to different neutron number $N$.
For a neutral atom, link the electron number to the proton number and check which statement must then be the same for both.
walkthrough: Identify what same element means: the proton number $Z$ is the same for both nuclei.
Recall the definition of isotopes: same $Z$ but different numbers of neutrons $N$, so different nucleon numbers $A = Z + N$.
Apply neutral-atom condition: in a neutral atom number of electrons equals number of protons $Z$.
Since $Z$ is common to both nuclides, the neutral atoms have the same number of electrons.

A.explanation: Same element means same proton number $Z$, so a neutral atom has the same number of electrons as protons in both nuclides.

B.explanation: Proton number $Z$ defines the element, so different isotopes of the same element have the same number of protons.

C.explanation: Nucleon number $A = Z + N$ is different for different isotopes because the neutron number is different.

D.explanation: Isotopes differ precisely in neutron number $N$, so the neutron numbers cannot be the same.
